classification.difficultyReason: Count restricted seating arrangements and compare them with all arrangements.

content.prompt: Three boys and three girls are to sit in a row. Find the probability that:

answer.worked:
There are $6!$ equally likely seating arrangements. The two alternating patterns are BGBGBG and GBGBGB. Within either pattern, the boys can be arranged in $3!$ ways and the girls in $3!$ ways.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{alternate})&=\frac{2\times3!\times3!}{6!}\\&=\frac{1}{10}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the boys sit together and the girls sit together,

answer.worked:
Treat the boys as one block and the girls as another. The two blocks can be arranged in $2!$ ways, with $3!$ arrangements within each block.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{both groups together})&=\frac{2!\times3!\times3!}{6!}\\&=\frac{1}{10}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: two specific girls sit next to one another.

answer.worked:
Treat the two specific girls as one block. Arrange this block and the other four people in $5!$ ways. The girls within the block can swap places in $2!$ ways.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{specified girls together})&=\frac{2!\times5!}{6!}\\&=\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}$$
